title: Endogenous retrovirus-derived RNA-DNA hybrids induce microglial synaptic pruning in autism models
authors: Shaoxuan Chen, Boxin Zhang, Tianyu Qin, Mengyue Zhu, Qiang Chen, Lu Xia, Huifang Pan, Qihua Yang, Shuanghui Guo, Rui Gong, Qiwu Jiang, Hongda Li, Xueqin Zhang, Pu Cheng, Xuchen Qi, Wei Chen, Wei Mo
abstract: Based on mouse models of MIA and Setdb1 deficiency, the study by Chen et al. identifies an ERV-mediated C4b-microglia pathway in autism. The authors propose that RTI intervention targeting ERV reverse transcription may modulate C4b-microglia activation and alleviate autism symptoms.

title: 20 years of concept cells: From invariant responses to a unique coding of human memory
abstract: Quian Quiroga summarizes findings with human single-neuron recordings and concept cells. He proposes that concept cells provide a key, uniquely human mechanism of memory storage that is not present in other species and supports human cognitive abilities and intelligence.

title: Before synapses are lost: Do endogenous retroviruses drive microglial overpruning in autism spectrum disorders?
abstract: Endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) are epigenetically silenced genomic elements whose reactivation can influence host gene regulation. In this issue of Neuron, Chen et al. identify ERV-derived RNA-DNA hybrids that activate neuronal C4b, driving microglial synaptic overpruning and autism-like behaviors.

abstract: Active dendrites enrich the repertoire of single-neuron computations. Whereas a lot is known about the function of dendrites in vitro, information about their in vivo properties is limited. title: Novelty beyond counting
abstract: Novelty signals guide learning and exploration. Becker et al. show that novelty depends not only on repetition but also on similarity: familiarity generalizes across related stimuli and states, explaining both cortical novelty responses in mouse V1 and novelty-driven maze exploration behavior.
